data.name: Red Rope: Don't Fall Behind
data.detailed_description:
Trading Cards


Acerca do jogo


Red Rope: Don’t Fall Behind is an allegorical local co-op game: the two protagonists are the archetypal couple, united by a rope that represents their bond.
Their link has a double meaning: it surely is a restriction, a promise, a limit to their liberty, but it is also an alliance, a pact, a synergy.
Without their link, the rope, they wouldn’t be able to survive the insidious labyrinth in which they move, they would be defenceless facing the macabre presences that torment them, they would be indiscernible from the roaming shadows they themselves sacrifice to strengthen their bond.
The labyrinth is a cosmological representation, a mandala, where every area, every enemy, every value and every geometry has an intentional symbolic placement.
What the players have to face is an initiatory journey in search of the key that opens the exit door.
An arduous and difficult challenge, a cathartic ritual, that only the most valiant players will be able to carry out, players with a special elective affinity.

Key Features:


  • Play with a friend or try alone. It won’t be easy either way.
  • You are trapped in a labyrinth: more than 100 hand-designed levels full of tension, action and mystery separate you from the exit.
  • The rope is the only weapon at your disposal.
  • Battle dozens of unpredictable enemies, learn their moves and plan yours. No tactics means death.
  • Solve puzzles: carefully observe and exploit the many mechanisms.
  • Discover a world packed with symbols to decipher and bizarre inhabitants.
  • Defeat 4 minibosses and 5 bosses on the path to triumph.
  • Climb the global chart but beware: every action has consequences.
  • The game continues beyond the screen: communication and complicity are paramount.
  • At least 10 hours of gameplay. Or 100 if you are not up to the challenge.
  • A true hardcore experience: only a few will succeed.

data.short_description: Red Rope is a terrifying, enigmatic adventure for 1 or 2 players who want to test their bond. Explore the Labyrinth, get acquainted with its bizarre inhabitants, its secrets and its rules. Face enemies, traps, puzzles, and ferocious bosses. Only the best will find the way out and become heroes.

reviews.review:
For 25 years now me and my gamer friends play cooperative games. Many duos and a lot of group coop gaming, we even once had a hobby coop-game site. I think we played most of the older coop games and are always looking for creative, outstanding and innovative coop games and we appreciate challenge and friction and games that make you engage with the game itself but also with how you act as a team. 

Red Rope is – hands-down - one of the best 2p coop games there is! It excels in absolutely every metric: 
Beautiful pixel graphics and a very distinct visual style that is goth and renaissance style and cosy as well as horror. I don’t even know how that makes sense but it does and big part of this successful atmosphere is the music.
 
The presentation is really flawless but is even getting overshadowed by the gameplay. This is coop through and through – one mistake is killing you and it does not even matter which partner contacts the enemy, easily the other partner could be at fault because they carelessly yanked you into the enemy or the other way around. You have to grow and learn as a team to know how to approach ever escalating, very creatively designed situations, how your partner is likely moving in a tense situation and how you can adapt to your partner to be better as a whole. The whole rope and sling your enemy mechanic is brilliant and behaves so differently depending how long your rope is. It really is cool how you get an instinctive feel for this. 

The level design is also top notch. Carefully crafted one screen challenge rooms and cleverly connected between each other. The whole 100 lives (plus some you collect or buy) economy to defeat the whole game is daunting but really onboards you well to the intense challenges and makes you evaluate your performance every time you are at a save game opportunity.
  
We died a lot and I expect every duo to play this to die often as well. We restarted three times over 7 years we played that game. We got better every time. We learned to appreciate the save-system and what a decision to save means. We also experienced how our skills grew by going through an are for 2,5 hours, losing 50 lives and be quite deflated to load again from the beginning and breezing through it in 25 minutes losing only 15 lives. Understanding the different enemy types (we really learned to hate some and dominated others) and the challenge of each area and room makes you so much more confident and capable.
 
We succeeded in the end (in a little over 8 hours) and we plan to meet for another weekend to make a mop up tour of remaining bosses and collectibles, just because we love this game so much and we do not want to let it go – so we are going for some more achievements!
 
I was asked if the game changed my relationship to my coop partner and to be honest: yes, it did. Having such a difficult and demanding project with one person over several years and being able to grow together, not get annoyed with each other’s mistakes and overcome all challenges that seem insurmountable at first, really is nice and tied us closer together (you know, like with a rope. A red rope). 

We had an absolutely great time and cannot recommend this enough for coop duos that really want to play an intense, beautiful and rewarding coop experience.  Easily among the most clear 10/10 true coop - experiences and should not be missed! 

The only sad thing is that we always were extra motivated to finish this because the dev team offered succesful duos (there seem to be not that many) to be pixelated and integrated into the game and announced over social media. We were looking forward to this but after so many years this seems to be no longer the case which is a bummer :(
